home.summary: The home is inviolable and private property is guaranteed by the Constitution.

properties.explanation: The home is inviolable and private property is guaranteed by the Constitution.
Entry into a home is allowed only with consent, by court order, or in the urgent cases the law lists.

representative.note: The people in a home decide for themselves; representation does not apply.

individual.summary: Personal autonomy is protected by the Constitution.

properties.explanation: Property is guaranteed and private property is inviolable; privacy and the home are inviolable.
These rights can be restricted by statute on the grounds the Constitution allows, e.g. entry into a home with consent or by court order.

representative.note: Individuals decide for themselves; representation does not apply.

business.summary: People can start a business and govern it themselves through the owners' meeting and the managers they elect.

properties.explanation: Anyone may start and run a business.
Licensing and permit regimes restrict entry into many activities.
Owners (shareholders, partners) decide in a general meeting.
Its resolutions bind the company.
Owners decide the company's statutes, profits and leadership.
The company controls its own capital and income.
Owners elect the managers or board.
Managers and board members are elected individually.
The owners can dismiss them.

nonprofit.summary: People can form non-profit associations and foundations and govern them through a members' assembly and an elected board.

properties.explanation: People may freely form associations and foundations.
Registration and, for public-benefit status, supervision by the state.
Members decide in a general assembly.
Its decisions bind the organisation.
Members adopt the statutes and elect the board.
Funded by members, donors and grants; tax relief depends on public-benefit status.
The members elect a board.
The members can dismiss the board.

entrance.summary: Owners can organise a condominium per entrance, with a general assembly of owners and an elected management board. Quorum is low and falls to zero on the next day.

properties.explanation: Where a building has more than one entrance, it can be managed separately for each entrance.
Decisions of the general assembly bind owners, users and occupants, including new ones.
51% of ideal shares must be present; after one hour 26% suffice; if still not, the meeting is held the next day with whoever attends.
Owners holding at least 20% of the ideal shares can require the meeting to be convened.
The assembly adopts the house rules, budget, contributions, the repair plan, loans and the use of common areas.
The assembly sets the contributions to the repair and renovation fund.
The executive body is a management board or a single manager.
The board implements the assembly's decisions and manages the common parts.
Board members are elected individually by the general assembly.
The term is up to two years, and the general assembly can end it early for failure to perform.

building.summary: Same regime as for an entrance: the Condominium Management Act applies to the building, or separately to each entrance.

neighbourhood.summary: A district (район) can hold a citizen-initiated local referendum; a smaller quarter (квартал) that is not a district or кметство cannot. A general assembly is possible but needs one quarter of residents to attend and is not directly binding. Municipal councillors are elected from municipality-wide party lists, so no councillor answers to the quarter.

properties.explanation: A local referendum can be held for a district (район) of Sofia, Plovdiv or Varna, as well as for a municipality or кметство.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
1. a referendum;

items.ref: Chapter II – Referendum, Section III – Local referendum

items.text: A local referendum shall be held in a municipality, district (район) or mayoralty (кметство) to decide directly on matters of local importance that the law has placed within the competence of the bodies of local self-government or of the bodies of the district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: The decision needs no later approval by the municipal council; it takes effect when announced and the mayor organises its implementation.

items.text: A decision adopted by local referendum shall not be subject to subsequent approval by the municipal council. The council shall adopt an act where necessary for its implementation.
A decision adopted by local referendum shall enter into force immediately upon its announcement.
The implementation of a decision adopted by local referendum shall be organised by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: Held on its own, a local referendum needs at least 40% turnout (a participation quorum). Held together with local elections, it needs “yes” votes from more than half of those voting in the council election instead (an approval quorum), which is less fatal. But whether it is held with the elections is up to the municipal council, which sets the date.

items.text: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if no fewer than 40 per cent of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality have taken part in it and more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.fix: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the 40% turnout quorum: the majority of those who vote decides.

items.text: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the valid votes cast in the respective municipality in the elections for municipal councillors have answered “yes”.
items.fix: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the approval quorum tied to the number of election voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall set the date for holding the referendum no earlier than 45 days and no later than 60 days after the decision on the referendum.
The municipal council shall set the date of voting on a non-working day. When several proposals have been received, the municipal council shall set a common date for holding the local referendum.

properties.explanation: Voters answer a question with yes or no; they do not vote on a drafted text such as an ordinance or a law.

items.text: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions.
items.fix: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions, or on a draft decision, ordinance or other act within the competence of the municipal council, which, if approved, takes effect as worded.
items.why: Lets voters approve a drafted decision or ordinance, which then takes effect as worded.

properties.explanation: 1/20 of voters to propose. The council is obliged to call it only with 1/10 of voters, which in Sofia means well over 100,000 signatures.

text: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one twentieth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
fix: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one hundredth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
items.why: Lowers the signatures needed to propose a local referendum from 1/20 to 1/100 of voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one tenth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty, and it does not contravene the restriction under Article 26(2).
items.fix: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty.
items.why: Lowers the signatures that oblige the council to call it from 1/10 to 1/50 of voters, and drops the topic restriction.

items.text: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within three months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.fix: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within six months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.why: Gives the initiative committee six months instead of three to collect signatures.

properties.explanation: The municipal budget, the size of local taxes and fees, and the council’s internal rules cannot be put to a local referendum.

text: The following questions may not be decided by local referendum:
1. the municipal budget;
2. the size of local taxes and fees;
3. the rules of the internal organisation and activity of the municipal council.
fix: (repealed)
items.why: Lifts the ban on local referendums about the budget, local taxes and fees, and the council's rules.

properties.explanation: If the council's term ends before it decides on a petition, the law does not say the procedure continues before the next council, so the petition can lapse.

items.fix: If the term of office of the municipal council ends before it has decided on a petition submitted under Article 27(2), the procedure shall continue before the newly elected council, which shall decide on the petition within one month of its first session.
items.why: A petition no longer lapses when the council's term ends.

properties.explanation: A veto referendum exists only for the whole municipality (Art. 27(3)); a village or quarter cannot veto a decision that concerns only it.

items.fix: When a decision of the municipal council concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the procedure under paragraph 3 may be initiated with the signatures of one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights there, and the referendum shall be held in that district, mayoralty or quarter.
items.why: Lets a district, village or quarter veto a council decision that concerns only it.

properties.explanation: The law does not provide this kind of referendum.

items.fix: Decisions of the municipal council on new non-recurring expenditure exceeding 5 per cent of the annual budget, on long-term municipal debt, and on the disposal of municipal property of public importance shall take effect only after their approval by local referendum. When such a decision concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the referendum shall be held there.
items.why: Sends large spending, debt and sales of public property to the voters automatically.

mechanisms.name: General assembly of the population (общо събрание на населението)

properties.explanation: Only quarters (квартали) and districts of up to 10,000 inhabitants can hold one, which rules out most city neighbourhoods.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
4. a general assembly of the population.

items.ref: Chapter IV – General assembly of the population

items.text: A general assembly of the population shall be held to decide matters of local importance which, on grounds of expediency, fall within the competence of the respective municipal council or mayor.
A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters with a population of up to 10,000 inhabitants.
items.fix: A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters.
items.why: Removes the 10,000-inhabitant limit on general assemblies.

properties.explanation: Not directly binding: the municipal council or mayor must issue the acts that implement it within one month.

items.text: The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
items.fix: The decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty shall be binding. The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to implement it within one month of its adoption, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
items.why: Makes the assembly's decision binding; the council and mayor only implement it.

items.text: The municipal council shall take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter.
items.fix: The decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter shall be binding. The municipal council shall issue the relevant acts to implement it within one month of its adoption.
items.why: Makes the assembly's decision binding in settlements and quarters too.

items.text: On the basis of the decision of the general assembly, the mayor shall, within 7 days, issue an order specifying the measures for its implementation, or submit a proposal to the municipal council for the preparation and adoption of a relevant decision, rules or ordinance.

properties.explanation: One quarter of eligible voters must attend (one third in places of up to 150 inhabitants). If not, after one hour it may proceed only with one tenth. In a quarter of 10,000 that is 1,000 people in one room.

items.text: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate if no fewer than one quarter of the citizens with voting rights in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter are present.
items.fix: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate whatever the number of citizens with voting rights present, provided it has been convened and announced as this Act requires.
items.why: Removes the attendance quorum: those who come decide.

items.text: In settlements with up to 150 inhabitants, at least one third of the citizens with voting rights in the settlement must be present for a general assembly of the population to be held.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the stricter quorum for small settlements.

items.text: If the required number of citizens has not appeared at the set time, the assembly shall be postponed by one hour, after which it shall be held with those present. Their number, however, may not be less than one tenth of all citizens with voting rights.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the fallback quorum of one tenth.

properties.explanation: The mayor must convene it on request of 1/50 of eligible voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

items.text: The initiative committee shall submit the petition to the mayor, who shall be obliged to convene the general assembly of the population within the period stated in it.
The general assembly shall be held no earlier than 15 days and no later than one month after it has been announced.

properties.explanation: 1/50 of voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

properties.explanation: The law provides no elected body for a neighbourhood (квартал). Districts (райони) of Sofia, Plovdiv and Varna elect only a district mayor, who carries out municipal decisions; there are no district councils.

items.text: The constituent administrative-territorial units within municipalities are mayoralties (кметства) and districts (райони). They are created under conditions and by a procedure laid down by law.
items.fix: The constituent administrative-territorial units within municipalities are mayoralties (кметства), districts (райони) and quarters (квартали). They are created under conditions and by a procedure laid down by law.
items.why: Makes quarters units of local self-government.

items.text: Mayors of districts are elected in the districts of Sofia Municipality and of cities divided into districts.
items.fix: Mayors and councils of districts are elected in the districts of Sofia Municipality and of cities divided into districts. Quarter councils are elected in quarters.
items.why: Gives districts and quarters elected councils of their own.

text: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the municipal budget in its part for the district or mayoralty;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. is responsible for managing municipal property sites designated by the municipal council;
11. organises the implementation of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality relating to the territory and citizens of the district or mayoralty;
12. performs functions assigned by the mayor of the municipality.
fix: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the budget of the district or mayoralty adopted by its council;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. manages the municipal property located in the district or mayoralty and serving its residents;

11. organises the implementation of the acts of the council of the district or mayoralty, and of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality on matters of municipal importance;
12. (repealed)
items.why: The district or mayoralty mayor implements its own council's decisions and budget.

mechanisms.name: Own member of the municipal council

properties.explanation: The whole municipality is one constituency, so no councillor is elected by, or answers to, the neighbourhood.

items.text: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality constitutes one multi-member constituency.
items.fix: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality is divided into constituencies of three to five seats each, which follow the boundaries of its districts, mayoralties and quarters.
items.why: Splits the municipality into districts of 3 to 5 seats along districts, mayoralties and quarters.

items.text: The results of the voting for municipal councillors under the proportional system are determined by the Hare-Niemeyer method.
items.fix: The results of the voting for municipal councillors are determined by the single transferable vote.
items.why: Replaces the Hare-Niemeyer list count with STV.

fix: In settlements that are not the administrative centre of a mayoralty, the residents elect mayoral deputies (кметски наместници) for the term of office.
Mayoral deputies are bodies of executive power in the settlement. They may be dismissed early only on the grounds laid down by law.
items.why: Residents elect their mayoral deputy, who can no longer be dismissed at will.

properties.explanation: The кметство mayor only carries out the municipal budget and the council’s and municipal mayor’s acts for the village, with an advisory vote in the council. The municipal council sets the mayor’s powers and decides the budget, fees, property and plans, so the village cannot govern most of its own interests. No own budget: the municipal council sets the кметство's budget figures.

text: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the municipal budget in its part for the district or mayoralty;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. is responsible for managing municipal property sites designated by the municipal council;
11. organises the implementation of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality relating to the territory and citizens of the district or mayoralty;
12. performs functions assigned by the mayor of the municipality.
fix: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the budget of the district or mayoralty adopted by its council;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. manages the municipal property located in the district or mayoralty and serving its residents;

11. organises the implementation of the acts of the council of the district or mayoralty, and of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality on matters of municipal importance;
12. (repealed)
items.why: The district or mayoralty mayor implements its own council's decisions and budget.

items.text: The mayor of a district and the mayor of a mayoralty may take part in the sessions of the municipal council in an advisory capacity. They must be heard when matters concerning the mayoralty or district are discussed.

text: The municipal council:

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, including the figures for the districts, mayoralties and settlements with mayoral deputies, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property and determines the specific powers of the mayor of the municipality and of the mayors of districts and mayoralties;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the exclusive competence of other bodies.

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it; the districts and mayoralties adopt their own budgets from the revenues assigned to them by law;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property, except property located in a district or mayoralty and serving its residents, which is managed by that district or mayoralty;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the competence of districts, mayoralties or other bodies.

items.ref: Chapter II – Referendum, Section III – Local referendum

items.text: A local referendum shall be held in a municipality, district (район) or mayoralty (кметство) to decide directly on matters of local importance that the law has placed within the competence of the bodies of local self-government or of the bodies of the district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: The decision needs no later approval by the municipal council; it takes effect when announced and the mayor organises its implementation.

items.text: A decision adopted by local referendum shall not be subject to subsequent approval by the municipal council. The council shall adopt an act where necessary for its implementation.
A decision adopted by local referendum shall enter into force immediately upon its announcement.
The implementation of a decision adopted by local referendum shall be organised by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: Held on its own, a local referendum needs at least 40% turnout (a participation quorum). Held together with local elections, it needs “yes” votes from more than half of those voting in the council election instead (an approval quorum), which is less fatal. But whether it is held with the elections is up to the municipal council, which sets the date.

items.text: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if no fewer than 40 per cent of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality have taken part in it and more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.

items.why: Removes the 40% turnout quorum: the majority of those who vote decides.

items.text: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the valid votes cast in the respective municipality in the elections for municipal councillors have answered “yes”.
items.fix: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the approval quorum tied to the number of election voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall set the date for holding the referendum no earlier than 45 days and no later than 60 days after the decision on the referendum.

properties.explanation: Voters answer a question with yes or no; they do not vote on a drafted text such as an ordinance or a law.

items.text: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions.
items.fix: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions, or on a draft decision, ordinance or other act within the competence of the municipal council, which, if approved, takes effect as worded.
items.why: Lets voters approve a drafted decision or ordinance, which then takes effect as worded.

properties.explanation: 1/20 of voters to propose. The council is obliged to call it only with 1/10 of voters, which in Sofia means well over 100,000 signatures.

text: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one twentieth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.

items.text: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one tenth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty, and it does not contravene the restriction under Article 26(2).
items.fix: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty.
items.why: Lowers the signatures that oblige the council to call it from 1/10 to 1/50 of voters, and drops the topic restriction.

items.text: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within three months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.fix: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within six months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.why: Gives the initiative committee six months instead of three to collect signatures.

fix: (repealed)
items.why: Lifts the ban on local referendums about the budget, local taxes and fees, and the council's rules.

items.why: Lowers the veto signatures to 1/50, gives two months to collect them, and suspends the decision until the vote.

mechanisms.name: General assembly of the population (общо събрание на населението)

properties.explanation: Only municipalities of up to 10,000 inhabitants can hold one.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
4. a general assembly of the population.

items.ref: Chapter IV – General assembly of the population

items.text: A general assembly of the population shall be held to decide matters of local importance which, on grounds of expediency, fall within the competence of the respective municipal council or mayor.
A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters with a population of up to 10,000 inhabitants.
items.fix: A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters.
items.why: Removes the 10,000-inhabitant limit on general assemblies.

properties.explanation: Not directly binding: the municipal council or mayor must issue the acts that implement it within one month.

items.text: The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
items.fix: The decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty shall be binding. The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to implement it within one month of its adoption, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
items.why: Makes the assembly's decision binding; the council and mayor only implement it.

items.text: The municipal council shall take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter.
items.fix: The decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter shall be binding. The municipal council shall issue the relevant acts to implement it within one month of its adoption.
items.why: Makes the assembly's decision binding in settlements and quarters too.

items.text: On the basis of the decision of the general assembly, the mayor shall, within 7 days, issue an order specifying the measures for its implementation, or submit a proposal to the municipal council for the preparation and adoption of a relevant decision, rules or ordinance.

properties.explanation: One quarter of eligible voters must attend (one third in places of up to 150 inhabitants). If not, after one hour it may proceed only with one tenth. In a quarter of 10,000 that is 1,000 people in one room.

items.text: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate if no fewer than one quarter of the citizens with voting rights in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter are present.
items.fix: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate whatever the number of citizens with voting rights present, provided it has been convened and announced as this Act requires.
items.why: Removes the attendance quorum: those who come decide.

items.text: In settlements with up to 150 inhabitants, at least one third of the citizens with voting rights in the settlement must be present for a general assembly of the population to be held.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the stricter quorum for small settlements.

items.text: If the required number of citizens has not appeared at the set time, the assembly shall be postponed by one hour, after which it shall be held with those present. Their number, however, may not be less than one tenth of all citizens with voting rights.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the fallback quorum of one tenth.

properties.explanation: Not met. Voters must first choose a party list, and a preference is optional. Only one preference is allowed, with no ranking as in the single transferable vote. A vote without a preference counts as a preference for the first candidate on the list, which, together with the 7% threshold, makes it almost impossible to replace that candidate.

items.text: When voting for the candidate list of a party or coalition, the voter may mark one preference for a candidate on the list, thereby expressing a preference as to the order of the candidates on the list voted for.
items.fix: When voting, the voter may rank as many candidates as they wish in order of preference, by marking 1, 2, 3 and so on beside their names, regardless of the party, coalition or committee that nominated them.
items.why: Lets voters rank council candidates of any party, instead of one preference within a list.

items.text: The vote is valid for the candidate list even if no preference has been marked for a candidate from the list of the party or coalition voted for.
items.fix: The vote is valid if at least one candidate has been marked with the number 1.
items.why: A vote counts for a person, not for a list.

items.text: Where the voter has not marked a preference for a candidate on the chosen candidate list, a preference is counted for the candidate placed first on the list.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Ends the rule that gives unmarked preferences to the list's first candidate.

items.text: Preferences for individual candidates are valid if the number of votes received for the candidate is no less than 7 per cent of the votes cast for the candidate list.
items.fix: Candidates are elected by the single transferable vote: each ballot counts for the voter's highest-ranked candidate who can still use it, and surplus and eliminated candidates' votes are transferred by the voters' next preferences until all seats are filled.
items.why: Replaces the 7% preference threshold with STV counting.

items.why: A petition no longer lapses when parliament dissolves or its term ends.

properties.explanation: Citizens cannot call a vote to overturn a decision once it has been adopted.

fix: (1) If, within 100 days of the promulgation of a law, an initiative committee submits a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than 50,000 citizens with voting rights, the law shall be put to a national referendum.
(2) The law shall not enter into force before the referendum. It shall be deemed rejected if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have voted “no”.
items.why: Lets citizens call a vote on any new law before it takes effect.

properties.explanation: The law does not require any decision to go to a vote automatically.

items.fix: Laws amending the Constitution, and decisions to ratify international treaties that transfer powers of the State, shall enter into force only after their approval by national referendum.
items.why: Sends the most fundamental decisions to the voters automatically.

properties.explanation: Not met. Voters must first choose a party list, and a preference is optional. Only one preference is allowed, with no ranking as in the single transferable vote; a ballot with more than one counts for the list only. A vote without a preference counts as a preference for the first candidate on the list, which, together with the 7% threshold, makes it almost impossible to replace that candidate. In practice, only about 3% of members of parliament have been elected thanks to preference votes.

items.text: Elections for members of parliament are held under a proportional electoral system, with candidate lists of parties and coalitions, or of initiative committees, registered in multi-member constituencies.
items.fix: Elections for members of parliament are held under the single transferable vote, in multi-member constituencies of three to five seats.
items.why: Replaces party lists with the single transferable vote in districts of 3 to 5 seats.

items.text: When voting for the candidate list of a party or coalition, the voter may mark one preference for a candidate on the list, thereby expressing a preference as to the order of the candidates on the list voted for.
items.fix: When voting, the voter may rank as many candidates as they wish in order of preference, by marking 1, 2, 3 and so on beside their names, regardless of the party, coalition or committee that nominated them.
items.why: Lets voters rank candidates of any party, instead of one preference within a list.

text: The vote is valid for the candidate list even if no preference has been marked for a candidate from the list of the party or coalition voted for.
If more than one preference has been marked, the ballot is taken to contain no preference, and the vote counts only for the chosen candidate list.
fix: The vote is valid if at least one candidate has been marked with the number 1.
(repealed)
items.why: A vote counts for a person, not for a list.

items.text: Where the voter has not marked a preference for a candidate on the chosen candidate list, a preference is counted for the candidate placed first on the list.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Ends the rule that gives unmarked preferences to the list's first candidate.

items.text: Preferences for individual candidates are valid if the number of votes received for the candidate is no less than 7 per cent of the votes cast for the candidate list.
items.fix: Candidates are elected by the single transferable vote: each ballot counts for the voter's highest-ranked candidate who can still use it, and surplus and eliminated candidates' votes are transferred by the voters' next preferences until all seats are filled.
items.why: Replaces the 7% preference threshold with STV counting.

properties.explanation: 31 multi-member districts matching the regions (Sofia split in three, Plovdiv in two).

items.text: For the elections, the territory of the country is divided into 31 multi-member constituencies, including three in Sofia City and two in Plovdiv region. The other constituencies coincide with the boundaries of the regions of the country.
items.fix: For the elections, the territory of the country is divided into constituencies of three to five seats each, with about the same number of voters per seat, following the boundaries of municipalities and regions where possible.
items.why: Draws smaller districts of 3 to 5 seats, so each area has its own representatives.

union.summary: The European citizens' initiative is not binding. Bulgarian MEPs are elected from one national list.
